items.subtype: sentence fragment vs. independent clause (missing finite verb)
items.stem: ___ nutrients from the soil through networks of fine root hairs.
items.answer_explanation: Only option A supplies both a subject ('Young seedlings') and a finite verb ('absorb'), producing a complete independent clause; the other options fail to form a grammatical main clause.

distractor_rationales.A: correct — provides a full subject + finite verb, forming a complete independent clause.
distractor_rationales.B: fragment — 'Absorbing' is a present participle with no finite verb, so the sentence never gets a main verb.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — the verb 'Absorb' has no subject, leaving the clause without a required subject.
distractor_rationales.D: wrong_word_order — the adjective 'young' is placed after the noun it modifies ('Seedlings young') instead of before it.

items.subtype: restrictive relative clause with correct relative pronoun (object gap)
items.stem: The arctic tern, a seabird ___ for a decade, completes one of the longest migrations of any bird.
items.answer_explanation: Option B uses the correct relative pronoun 'that' for a non-human antecedent together with the correctly formed present perfect verb 'have tracked' in an object-gap restrictive clause.

distractor_rationales.A: incorrect_relative_marker — 'who' is reserved for human antecedents; the non-human 'seabird' requires 'that' or 'which'.
distractor_rationales.B: correct — correct relative pronoun and correctly formed present perfect verb for an object-gap restrictive clause.
distractor_rationales.C: double_subject — the resumptive pronoun 'they' redundantly repeats the subject 'scientists' already present in the clause.
distractor_rationales.D: wrong_verb_form — 'have track' should be 'have tracked'; a past participle is required after 'have'.

items.subtype: reduced passive relative clause (past participle modifying noun)
items.stem: Pottery fragments ___ along the banks of an ancient river have provided evidence that early trade networks once linked distant communities.
items.answer_explanation: Option C is a correctly formed reduced passive relative clause ('fragments [that were] unearthed by archaeologists') modifying 'fragments'.

distractor_rationales.A: wrong_voice — the active present participle 'unearthing' wrongly implies the fragments themselves are doing the unearthing.
distractor_rationales.B: missing_required_element — the preposition 'by', which introduces the passive agent, is missing, making 'archaeologists' look like a direct object.
distractor_rationales.C: correct — a past participle plus a correctly placed agent phrase forms a standard reduced passive relative clause.
distractor_rationales.D: wrong_word_order — the agent phrase 'by archaeologists' is placed before the participle instead of after it.

items.subtype: appositive noun phrase placement and internal word order
items.stem: Rembrandt, ___, painted dozens of self-portraits throughout his career.

options.A: master a Dutch of light and shadow
options.B: a a Dutch master of light and shadow
options.C: who a Dutch master of light and shadow
options.D: a Dutch master of light and shadow

items.answer_explanation: Option D is a correctly ordered appositive noun phrase ('a Dutch master of light and shadow') renaming 'Rembrandt'.

distractor_rationales.A: wrong_word_order — the article and noun are scrambled ('master a Dutch' instead of 'a Dutch master').
distractor_rationales.B: extraneous_element — the article 'a' is duplicated ('a a Dutch master').
distractor_rationales.C: fragment — inserting 'who' without a verb (e.g., 'who was') leaves the inserted clause without a finite verb.
distractor_rationales.D: correct — a standard appositive noun phrase in the correct internal word order.

items.subtype: predicate nominative after linking verb (be + NP)
items.stem: Inflation ___ the sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services within an economy.
items.answer_explanation: Option A correctly completes the linking verb 'is' with a predicate nominative ('a measure') followed by the required preposition 'of'.

distractor_rationales.A: correct — a full predicate nominative noun phrase properly completes the linking verb 'is'.
distractor_rationales.B: incorrect_part_of_speech — the adverb 'measurably' cannot serve as the predicate complement of a linking verb, which requires a noun or adjective.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — the article 'a' before 'measure' is missing.
distractor_rationales.D: wrong_complementation — the passive-style participle 'measured' combined with 'to' does not supply the predicate-nominative structure the linking verb requires.

items.subtype: embedded question (wh-word) word order
items.stem: Linguists have long debated ___ shapes the cognitive categories that speakers use to perceive the world around them.

options.A: whether does the structure of a language actually
options.B: whether the structure of a language actually
options.C: the structure of a language actually

items.answer_explanation: Option B forms a correctly ordered embedded question: 'whether' introduces the noun clause, and the clause keeps normal statement word order (subject 'the structure of a language' before the verb 'shapes').

distractor_rationales.A: wrong_word_order — inserting the auxiliary 'does' and inverting the subject imports direct-question word order into an embedded clause, which must keep statement order.
distractor_rationales.B: correct — 'whether' plus normal statement word order correctly forms the embedded question.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — the subordinator 'whether' is missing, leaving no word to introduce the embedded clause.
distractor_rationales.D: fragment — dropping the head noun 'structure' leaves the clause with no subject for the verb 'shapes'.

items.subtype: non-restrictive relative clause with parallel coordinate predicate
items.stem: Basalt, ___ much of the ocean floor, forms when molten lava cools rapidly at the surface and hardens into solid rock.

options.A: who originates deep within the mantle and covers
options.B: which originates deep within the mantle and it covers
options.C: which originates deep within the mantle and covers
options.D: which originates deep within the mantle and covering

items.answer_explanation: Option C uses the correct relative pronoun 'which' for the inanimate antecedent 'Basalt' and keeps the two coordinate verbs ('originates' and 'covers') in parallel finite form sharing the same subject.

distractor_rationales.A: incorrect_relative_marker — 'who' is used for human antecedents; the inanimate 'Basalt' requires 'which' or 'that'.
distractor_rationales.B: extraneous_element — the inserted pronoun 'it' unnecessarily duplicates the subject already carried by 'which', breaking the coordinate structure.
distractor_rationales.C: correct — correct relative pronoun with two parallel finite verbs sharing one subject.
distractor_rationales.D: wrong_verb_form — the gerund 'covering' breaks parallelism with the finite verb 'originates' in the coordinated predicate.

items.subtype: contrast connector selection (although vs. despite vs. however)
items.stem: ___ forecasters had predicted clear skies for the entire weekend, a sudden storm system moved through the region without warning.
items.answer_explanation: Option D, 'Although', correctly signals a concessive relation between the forecasters' prediction and the unexpected storm.

distractor_rationales.A: incorrect_subordinator — 'Because' signals a causal relation, not the concessive relation the sentence requires.
distractor_rationales.B: extraneous_element — 'Even although' is a nonstandard combination; 'even' is not licensed together with 'although'.
distractor_rationales.C: wrong_word_order — the fixed expression 'even though' has its elements reversed ('though even').
distractor_rationales.D: correct — 'Although' is the standard subordinating conjunction for a concessive relation.

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across intervening phrase
items.stem: The depth of the ocean's deepest trenches ___ nearly eleven kilometers at its most extreme point.
items.answer_explanation: The singular subject 'depth' requires the singular verb 'reaches', regardless of the intervening plural noun 'trenches'.

distractor_rationales.A: correct — singular verb correctly agrees with the singular subject 'depth'.
distractor_rationales.B: agreement_error — the plural verb 'reach' wrongly agrees with the nearby plural noun 'trenches' instead of the true subject 'depth'.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — there is no main verb at all; the clause needs a verb between the subject and the measurement.
distractor_rationales.D: fragment — the participle 'reaching' cannot serve as the sentence's finite verb, leaving the clause without one.

items.subtype: infinitive modifying ordinal/superlative noun ('the first...to')
items.stem: The team of anthropologists was the first ___ evidence of organized long-distance trade among hunter-gatherer communities that once inhabited the region.
items.answer_explanation: The superlative phrase 'the first' requires a following infinitive ('to uncover') to express the accomplishment.

distractor_rationales.A: incorrect_part_of_speech — a gerund ('uncovering') is used where the construction requires an infinitive.
distractor_rationales.B: correct — the infinitive 'to uncover' correctly follows the superlative 'the first'.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — the infinitive marker 'to' is missing before the base verb.
distractor_rationales.D: wrong_word_order — 'uncover' and 'to' are present but reversed; the marker 'to' must precede the verb.

items.subtype: adjective order within a noun phrase
items.stem: The orchestra performed a ___ symphony that had not been heard by a live audience in over a century.
items.answer_explanation: The opinion adjective 'rare' correctly precedes the age adjective 'eighteenth-century' with no coordinating conjunction needed between them.

distractor_rationales.A: wrong_word_order — the age adjective is placed before the opinion adjective, reversing the standard order.
distractor_rationales.B: extraneous_element — the conjunction 'and' is unnecessarily inserted between two cumulative adjectives that should not be coordinated.
distractor_rationales.C: correct — opinion adjective before age adjective, the standard order for stacked noun modifiers.
distractor_rationales.D: incorrect_part_of_speech — the adverb 'rarely' is used where an adjective is required to modify the noun 'symphony'.

items.subtype: object complement after causative verb (make + O + Adj)
items.stem: City planners hope that wider sidewalks and dedicated bike lanes will make the downtown corridor ___.

options.A: more accessibility for pedestrians and cyclists alike
options.B: for pedestrians and cyclists alike more accessible
options.D: more accessible for pedestrians and cyclists alike

items.answer_explanation: The causative verb 'make' requires an adjective object complement; 'more accessible for pedestrians and cyclists alike' correctly supplies that adjective plus its prepositional complement.

distractor_rationales.A: wrong_complementation — a noun phrase ('more accessibility') is used where the causative verb 'make' requires an adjective complement.
distractor_rationales.B: wrong_word_order — the prepositional phrase is moved before the adjective complement instead of following it.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — the preposition 'for', which links the adjective to its complement, is missing.
distractor_rationales.D: correct — adjective complement correctly followed by its prepositional phrase after the causative verb 'make'.

items.subtype: adjective + enough + to-infinitive result construction
items.stem: The greenhouse behind the botanical garden was ___ tropical orchids to bloom even in winter.
items.answer_explanation: The 'adjective + enough + for + noun + to-infinitive' pattern correctly expresses the result: the greenhouse was warm enough to permit the orchids to bloom.

distractor_rationales.A: wrong_degree_form — 'so' requires a following 'that'-clause, not a 'for...to' infinitive result phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: correct — 'enough' correctly follows the adjective, with 'for' introducing the logical subject of the infinitive.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — the preposition 'for', which introduces the infinitive's logical subject, is missing.
distractor_rationales.D: wrong_word_order — 'enough' must follow the adjective ('warm enough'), not precede it.

items.subtype: subject-auxiliary inversion after fronted negative adverbial ('Not until...')
items.stem: Not until the early twentieth century ___ the full extent of the ancient city's trade network with civilizations that lay far beyond its immediate borders.
items.answer_explanation: The fronted negative adverbial 'Not until the early twentieth century' triggers subject-auxiliary inversion, correctly produced by 'did archaeologists fully understand'.

distractor_rationales.A: correct — auxiliary 'did' correctly inverted before the subject after the fronted negative adverbial.
distractor_rationales.B: wrong_word_order — normal declarative order is used instead of the inversion required after a fronted negative adverbial.
distractor_rationales.C: missing_required_element — the auxiliary 'did' is missing entirely, so no inversion (or verb support) occurs.
distractor_rationales.D: double_subject — the pronoun 'they' redundantly repeats the subject 'archaeologists'.

items.subtype: parallel verb forms in a list
items.stem: Astronomers must analyze faint light signals, calculate vast distances, and ___ that reveal each galaxy's velocity.

options.B: interpretation of subtle shifts in color
options.D: and interpret subtle shifts in color

items.answer_explanation: The base verb 'interpret' correctly matches the parallel base-form verbs 'analyze' and 'calculate' in the coordinated list.

distractor_rationales.A: wrong_word_order — the adjective 'subtle' is placed after the noun it modifies ('shifts subtle') instead of before it.
distractor_rationales.B: incorrect_part_of_speech — a noun phrase ('interpretation of') is used where the parallel list requires a base-form verb.
distractor_rationales.C: correct — a base-form verb parallel to 'analyze' and 'calculate' correctly completes the list.
distractor_rationales.D: extraneous_element — the conjunction 'and' is duplicated, since the stem already supplies 'and' before the blank.

items.subtype: quantifier agreement with uncountable noun
items.sentence: According to the museum curator, many of the evidence displayed here was examined carefully by outside experts.
items.answer_explanation: "Evidence" is an uncountable noun, so it requires the quantifier "much," not "many," which is reserved for countable plural nouns.

items.subtype: pronoun with no clear antecedent
items.sentence: The observatory recently installed a sophisticated new spectrograph beside its aging telescope, and it will soon rival several professional facilities elsewhere.

marked_parts.A: recently installed a sophisticated new spectrograph

items.answer_explanation: The pronoun "it" could refer to "the observatory," "the spectrograph," or "the telescope," leaving its antecedent unclear; a specific noun phrase is needed to remove the ambiguity.

items.subtype: article selection with first-mention noun
items.sentence: Field geologists exploring a remote canyon recently discovered a unusual mineral formation attracting worldwide attention.

marked_parts.A: Field geologists exploring a remote canyon

items.answer_explanation: "Unusual" begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article before it must be "an," not "a."

items.subtype: pronoun-antecedent number mismatch
items.sentence: Marine biologists attached tracking devices to several dolphins living near the reef so that scientists could monitor its movements throughout migration season.

marked_parts.B: to several dolphins living near the reef

items.answer_explanation: The pronoun must agree in number with its plural antecedent "dolphins," so "their" is required instead of the singular "its."

items.subtype: quantifier agreement with countable plural noun
items.sentence: Much of the fossilized bones recovered from the quarry belonged to a previously unknown species of dinosaur.

marked_parts.D: a previously unknown species of dinosaur

items.answer_explanation: "Bones" is a countable plural noun, so the quantifier "many," not "much" (which modifies uncountable nouns), is required.

items.subtype: predicate adjective after linking verb misrendered as noun
items.sentence: Sociologists have found that prolonged unemployment often leaves individuals feeling isolation from their communities and support networks.

marked_parts.A: Sociologists have found that prolonged unemployment

items.answer_explanation: After the verb "feeling," a predicate adjective describing the individuals' state is required, so "isolated" (adjective) must replace the noun "isolation."

items.subtype: object complement after causative verb misrendered as adverb
items.sentence: The new legislation made the approval process considerably more efficiently, allowing agencies to issue permits within weeks.

marked_parts.D: allowing agencies to issue permits within weeks

items.answer_explanation: The causative verb "made" requires an adjective object complement describing "the approval process," so "efficient" is needed instead of the adverb "efficiently."

items.subtype: fixed preposition collocation governed by verb
items.sentence: Many contemporary philosophers who study ethics remain skeptical of arguments that rely heavily of intuition rather than rigorous analysis.

marked_parts.A: Many contemporary philosophers who study ethics
marked_parts.D: of intuition rather than rigorous analysis

items.minimal_correction: on intuition rather than rigorous analysis
items.answer_explanation: The verb "rely" takes the fixed preposition "on," not "of"; "rely on intuition" is the correct collocation.

items.subtype: parallel verb forms in a list (gerund vs. base form)
items.sentence: Measuring reaction rates precisely, to control temperature fluctuations, and to record every observation carefully are essential skills for any laboratory chemist.

marked_parts.C: and to record every observation carefully
marked_parts.D: are essential skills for any laboratory chemist

items.answer_explanation: The compound subject lists parallel infinitive phrases ("to control," "to record"), so the first item must also be an infinitive ("To measure") rather than the gerund "Measuring."

items.subtype: correlative conjunction parallelism (not only...but also)
items.sentence: The experiment not only confirmed the researchers' initial hypothesis but also were revealing unexpected patterns in the particle collisions that occurred at extremely high energies.

marked_parts.A: The experiment not only confirmed the researchers' initial hypothesis
marked_parts.B: but also were revealing unexpected patterns
marked_parts.D: that occurred at extremely high energies

items.answer_explanation: The correlative "not only...but also" requires parallel verb forms; since the first verb is simple past ("confirmed"), the second must also be simple past ("revealed"), not the past progressive "were revealing."

items.subtype: parallel noun phrases in enumeration, one item shifted to adjective
items.sentence: Botanists typically classify climbing plants according to their leaf shape, root structure, and stem flexible when studying adaptation to their environment.

marked_parts.B: according to their leaf shape, root structure,
marked_parts.D: when studying adaptation to their environment

items.answer_explanation: The list of three parallel noun phrases ("leaf shape," "root structure") requires a matching noun ("stem flexibility"), not the adjective "flexible."

items.subtype: gerund vs. infinitive complement selection after verb
items.sentence: After spotting several rare shorebirds nesting near the shoreline, the research team decided avoiding the nesting site entirely for the remainder of the season.

marked_parts.A: After spotting several rare shorebirds nesting near the shoreline
marked_parts.D: avoiding the nesting site entirely for the remainder of the season

items.minimal_correction: to avoid the nesting site entirely for the remainder of the season
items.answer_explanation: The verb "decided" requires an infinitive complement ("to avoid"), not the gerund "avoiding."

items.subtype: participial phrase of result mis-formed as finite clause fragment
items.sentence: Causes extensive soil erosion throughout the region, the prolonged drought forced many farmers to abandon their fields entirely last year.

marked_parts.A: Causes extensive soil erosion throughout the region
marked_parts.D: to abandon their fields entirely last year

items.minimal_correction: Causing extensive soil erosion throughout the region
items.answer_explanation: This fronted phrase functions as a participial phrase describing a result of the drought and must use the -ing participle "Causing," not the finite verb form "Causes," which has no subject of its own.

items.subtype: infinitive modifying superlative noun rendered as gerund
items.sentence: The young volcanologist was the first researcher studying the mountain's seismic tremors continuously, an effort that greatly improved eruption forecasting methods.

marked_parts.B: was the first researcher studying the mountain's seismic tremors continuously
marked_parts.D: that greatly improved eruption forecasting methods

items.minimal_correction: was the first researcher to study the mountain's seismic tremors continuously
items.answer_explanation: After an ordinal expression like "the first researcher," an infinitive ("to study") is required, not the gerund "studying."

items.subtype: adjective required, adverb used to modify a following noun
items.sentence: Early cartographers relying on approximately measurements and careful celestial observations still managed to draw coastlines with reasonable accuracy.

marked_parts.C: approximately measurements and careful celestial observations
marked_parts.D: still managed to draw coastlines with reasonable accuracy

items.minimal_correction: approximate measurements and careful celestial observations
items.answer_explanation: The noun "measurements" needs an adjective modifier ("approximate"), not the adverb "approximately."

items.subtype: adverb required, adjective used to modify a verb
items.sentence: During the outbreak, public health officials tracked new infections carefully and updated their containment strategies quick.

marked_parts.A: During the outbreak, public health officials

items.answer_explanation: The adverb "quickly," not the adjective "quick," is needed to modify the verb "updated."

items.subtype: noun required, adjective used as clause subject
items.sentence: Nutritious, according to many dietitians, plays a central role in preventing chronic disease and supporting long-term health.
items.answer_explanation: The clause subject must be the noun "nutrition," not the adjective "nutritious."

items.subtype: active voice used where passive is required (logical object as subject)
items.sentence: The old-growth forest has protected for over a century by strict conservation laws that limit logging and development.

marked_parts.B: has protected for over a century

items.minimal_correction: has been protected for over a century
items.answer_explanation: Because the forest is the recipient of the action described by the "by" phrase, the passive voice "has been protected" is required, not the active "has protected."

items.subtype: past perfect vs. simple past selection
items.sentence: By the time researchers finally identified the rare fungal species growing beneath the forest canopy, it already spread across nearly half of the reserve, threatening several native plant populations.

marked_parts.A: By the time researchers finally identified
marked_parts.B: the rare fungal species growing beneath the forest canopy,
marked_parts.C: it already spread across nearly half of the reserve,

items.minimal_correction: it had already spread across nearly half of the reserve,
items.answer_explanation: Because the spreading occurred before the researchers' identification, which is also in the past, the past perfect "had already spread" is required instead of the simple past "already spread."

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across intervening prepositional phrase
items.sentence: Entomologists studying colony organization note that the behavior of social insects such as ants and termites remain remarkably complex.

marked_parts.C: of social insects such as ants and termites

items.answer_explanation: The subject of the clause is the singular noun "behavior"; the intervening prepositional phrase "of social insects such as ants and termites" does not change the verb's number, so the singular verb "remains" is required.

items.subtype: missing required correlative element in a compound predicate
items.sentence: Not only ethnomusicologists study traditional instruments but also examine the cultural contexts in which they are played.

marked_parts.A: Not only ethnomusicologists study traditional instruments

items.minimal_correction: Not only do ethnomusicologists study traditional instruments
items.answer_explanation: A clause beginning with the correlative "Not only" requires subject-auxiliary inversion, so the auxiliary "do" must be inserted before the subject: "Not only do ethnomusicologists study..."

items.subtype: relative pronoun case (who/whom) selection
items.sentence: The weaver who historians credit with reviving an ancient dyeing technique trained dozens of apprentices throughout her long career in the textile guild.

marked_parts.B: who historians credit with reviving an ancient dyeing technique
marked_parts.D: throughout her long career in the textile guild

items.minimal_correction: whom historians credit with reviving an ancient dyeing technique
items.answer_explanation: The relative pronoun functions as the object of "credit" ("historians credit her"), so the objective case "whom" is required instead of the subjective "who."

items.subtype: verb agreement within a restrictive relative clause
items.sentence: Modern cryptographers rely on algorithms that processes enormous quantities of data within fractions of a second.

marked_parts.C: that processes enormous quantities of data

items.minimal_correction: that process enormous quantities of data
items.answer_explanation: The relative pronoun "that" refers back to the plural antecedent "algorithms," so the verb in the relative clause must be plural "process," not "processes."

items.subtype: wrong subordinating conjunction for concessive relation
items.sentence: The orchids still failed to bloom on schedule, because the greenhouse maintained nearly ideal humidity and temperature conditions throughout the season.

marked_parts.D: because the greenhouse maintained nearly ideal humidity and temperature conditions throughout the season

items.minimal_correction: although the greenhouse maintained nearly ideal humidity and temperature conditions throughout the season
items.answer_explanation: The clause describes a contrast (good conditions but failed blooming), so the concessive subordinator "although" is required instead of the causal "because," which incorrectly implies the good conditions caused the failure.

items.subtype: noun + postpositive adjective phrase word order
items.sentence: Prone regions to frequent earthquakes require strict building codes designed to minimize structural damage during sudden ground shaking.
items.answer_explanation: The adjective phrase "prone to frequent earthquakes" must follow the noun it modifies ("regions"), not precede it, so the correct order is "Regions prone to frequent earthquakes."
